interest: For historians of the Allied occupation of Japan and post-war agrarian reform, this file offers valuable insight into the U.S. inter-agency policymaking process connecting Washington committees (SWNCC/SANACC) to SCAP headquarters in Tokyo and the multilateral Far Eastern Commission. It illustrates the deliberate bureaucratic strategy of detaching cooperative and union democratization from contentious land-tenure reform to synchronize American policy with pending legislation in the Japanese Diet. Furthermore, the detailed historical discussion in Appendix B provides a candid U.S. assessment of how prewar Japanese agricultural associations and cooperatives had been co-opted into wartime state-controlled organs to mobilize the rural population, underscoring why American planners considered the establishment of genuinely autonomous, democratic grassroots farmers' organizations essential to preventing a resurgence of rural militarism and economic subjugation.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.5032) documents the formulation and inter-agency approval of United States occupation policy regarding the democratization of Japanese farmers' unions and cooperatives in late 1947. Originating from State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee paper SANACC 356/1 (and its amendment SANACC 356/2), the policy was separated from the broader agrarian and land reform paper (SWNCC 356) to ensure prompt guidance for the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) while relevant legislation was before the Japanese Diet. The file contains transmittal memoranda from SANACC Chairman Charles E. Saltzman to the Secretary of State, committee decisions amending the text, the complete underlying SANACC 356/1 report with historical analysis and policy appendices, and a transmittal memorandum by Deputy to the Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas Frank G. Wisner submitting the approved conclusions to the U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission for formal adoption. The policy mandates voluntary membership, democratic one-member-one-vote governance, financial autonomy, protection from governmental interference, the exclusion of purged wartime leaders and commercial competitors, access to non-discriminatory radio facilities and rural credit, and the dissolution of wartime compulsory agricultural associations.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a statement of United States policy on the democratization of Japanese farmers' unions and cooperatives for submission to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Frank G. Wisner, Deputy to the Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas, transmits a statement of United States policy regarding Japanese farmers' unions and cooperatives to the U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission. The policy statement comprises the Conclusions of SANACC 356/1, approved by the State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee on December 9, 1947. Wisner requests that the U.S. Member submit this statement to the Far Eastern Commission with a view to obtaining a formal policy decision.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frank G. Wisner to the U.S. Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Statement defining United States policy principles for fostering independent, voluntary, and democratic farmers' unions and cooperatives in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: This policy statement establishes principles for fostering democratic farmers' unions and cooperatives in Japan under the Japanese Constitution and occupation directives. It stipulates that membership must be voluntary, discrimination prohibited, and control based on one vote per member with patronage refunds. It bars business competitors and purged persons from office, guarantees civil liberties including non-discriminatory access to radio broadcasting, and protects cooperatives from government interference except during national emergencies. In addition, it recommends government provision of agricultural credit, technical guidance, and cooperative education, while requiring the abrogation of contrary wartime laws.
subfiles.title: Statement of United States Policy for Democratization of Japanese Farmers' Unions and Cooperatives

subfiles.about: Transmittal of approved copies of SANACC 356/1 regarding Japanese farmers' unions and cooperatives to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Charles E. Saltzman, Chairman of the State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee, forwards approved copies of SANACC 356/1 to the Secretary of State for appropriate action. The memorandum highlights recommendation paragraph 5a regarding transmission of the conclusions to the U.S. representative on the Far Eastern Commission. It also notes that the Joint Chiefs of Staff have been requested to forward the conclusions to SCAP for information, and requests copies of any implementing action taken by the Department of State.
subfiles.title: Memorandum SANA-5849 from Charles E. Saltzman to the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Secretariat notice recording the informal approval of amendments to SANACC 356/1 and circulating replacement pages.
subfiles.summary: This note by the SANACC Secretariat records that the State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee informally approved SANACC 356/1 as amended by SANACC 356/2 on December 9, 1947. It directs document holders to substitute revised pages 32, 33, 34, and 35 into their copies and to destroy superseded pages by burning. The notice is signed by Secretariat members V. L. Lowrance, V. F. Field, and J. P. Gardiner.
subfiles.title: Decision Amending SANACC 356/1: Policy for Democratization of Japanese Farmers' Unions and Cooperatives

subfiles.about: Comprehensive policy report setting forth recommendations, background facts, and historical analysis on democratizing Japanese agricultural organizations.
subfiles.from: State Member, State-Army-Navy-Air Force Coordinating Committee
subfiles.summary: This committee document circulates a State Member memorandum proposing to separate policy on Japanese farmers' unions and cooperatives from the broader land reform paper (SWNCC 356) for expedited approval and presentation to the Far Eastern Commission. The paper sets out conclusions establishing democratic operating principles for farmers' organizations and recommendations for transmitting them to the FEC and SCAP. Appendix A reviews relevant policy directives from the Potsdam Declaration to SCAP orders, while Appendix B surveys the prewar and wartime history of Japanese agricultural associations, tenant unions, and state regimentation, emphasizing the necessity of autonomous, democratic rural organizations.
subfiles.title: SANACC 356/1: Policy for Democratization of Japanese Farmers' Unions and Cooperatives
